extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary wire-service newspaper reporting of World War II events, combining datelined dispatches, official communiqués, broadcast reports, eyewitness anecdotes and leader quotations for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly attribute reports to the originating service or medium (e.g., "recorded here by The Associated Press", "broadcast, heard here by Reuters", "The communique, broadcast by the Berlin radio").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always identify the source and how the information was received (Associated Press dispatch, Rome radio broadcast, British broadcast, German communique, Navy statement). Example usages in this article: "The broadcast, heard here by Reuters","recorded here by The Associated Press","The communique, broadcast by the Berlin radio, said..." — include that wording so readers understand provenance and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label unconfirmed claims / note lack of confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag reports that lack independent verification (e.g., the page states: "There was no confirmation from Allied source").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When printing claims — especially those originating from enemy or partisan broadcasts — explicitly note the absence of confirmation ("no confirmation from Allied source") or that the government/agency has 'no comment'. Do not present unverified claims as established fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat broadcast/propaganda claims cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish propaganda or enemy radio claims from verified reporting (examples: Axis/Tōkio/Rome broadcasts claiming sinkings or actions, followed by Allied non-confirmation or the Navy's 'no comment').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute such claims clearly as broadcasts or propaganda, present them as claimed rather than established, and, where possible, await or seek corroboration from independent sources before treating them as factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use datelines and precise locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin dispatches with location and date (examples throughout: "LONDON, Feb. 1", "Somewhere in New Guinea, Feb. 1", "AUSTRALIA, Feb. 2 (Tuesday)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear dateline and location on each dispatch so readers know where and when the report originates; this helps contextualize the information and source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present official communiqués verbatim and by section
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting military or official communiqués, reproduce the text or numbered items and label theatres or sections (example: "Communique Number 267 said: 'South Pacific: 1. On January 28... 2. (a)... (b)... (c)...'").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote communiqués clearly, preserve their numbering and organization, and attribute them so readers can judge their origin; when the communique uses subheadings (theaters, numbered items), keep that structure in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote leaders and speeches with context
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotations from political or military leaders and state the circumstances of their remarks (examples: Mussolini's anniversary broadcast: "we shall return...", Doenitz's declaration: "I will put the entire strength of the Navy into the submarine war").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing leader statements, provide attribution (who, when, by what medium) and include key phrases verbatim to preserve meaning and allow readers to assess tone and intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report casualty/loss figures with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: When stating numbers of casualties, prisoners, ships sunk, or other losses, attribute the figures to their source (e.g., "Less than 43,000 men remain...", "totaling 3,227,008 tons had been sunk", "118 Americans rescued").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give numerical claims but always attach their provenance (communique, German dispatches, naval communique, Associated Press sources). If figures are estimates or claims, label them accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest and eyewitness detail to convey impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Enliven dispatches with vivid scene-setting and personal anecdotes (examples: "Streets littered with dead", pilot landing in a garden, marines sealing a cave), used alongside official reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine authoritative communiqués with on-the-ground descriptive details and small human stories to help readers grasp the scale and human dimension of events, while keeping such anecdotes clearly attributed and separated from official claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance opposing accounts and record official responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Give both claim and counterpoint where present: enemy claims followed by Allied statements or the absence of confirmation (example: Axis radio claims of sinkings; Allied 'no comment' and waits for own dispatches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple sides present differing accounts, report each with attribution and include official denials, 'no comment', or statements that the government/agency is awaiting verification, so readers see the contested nature of the facts.
